neighbours.label: the 'is' right before 'due' for an expected baby ('our first baby *is* due in March'). Weak on other announced arrivals ('which *is* to come', tournament seedings); rent or a report that 'is due' stays quiet.
fire: The main reason we moved in a hurry is that our second baby is due in April.
The actress told the magazine that her first baby is due in late September.
He wants the house finished by autumn because their third baby is due in November.
They postponed the trip because their first child is due in early June.
The couple confirmed to reporters that their second baby is due in January.
She plans to stop working in May since her baby is due in the middle of June.
The biggest reason to finish the nursery this month is that my first baby is due in February.
The singer cancelled the autumn tour because her second baby is due in October.
quiet: The main reason we moved in a hurry is that our rent is due in April.
The actress told the magazine that her first film was shot in late September.
He wants the house finished by autumn because the roof is leaking.
They postponed the trip because their first child is sick with the flu.
The couple confirmed to reporters that their second baby was born in January.
She plans to stop working in May since her contract is ending.
The biggest reason to finish the essay this month is that the final draft is due in February.
The singer cancelled the autumn tour because her voice is tired.

notes: Rare pole (0.078%). Top examples are copulas in news about something still to come: 'is the top seed', 'which is to come', 'she was pregnant', 'is expected to', 'my second baby is due'. Probes found only the baby case repeatable, and not strongly: 'baby is due' 0.23-0.55 in four of five sentences (0.08 in a short one), 'who is to come' 0.48 once and 0.00 once, 'is expected to' 0.02-0.05, seedings 0.13-0.14, 'report is due' 0.02, 'rent is due' 0.02. The label is the narrow case that reproduced, not an account of the pole; the median fire may fall short.
